title: Resource Hub shared definitions
description: Building blocks the other Resource Hub schemas reference: identifiers, slugs, and the lists of topic and type slugs that describe where a resource is listed. Nothing here is a payload on its own.

id.description: A WordPress object ID (post ID or term ID): a positive integer, never a string.

slug.description: A WordPress slug (post_name or term slug) as it appears in a URL path segment: non-empty, at most 200 characters (WordPress's post_name column width), with no slash and no whitespace. Any character set WordPress itself allows is accepted; the schema does not restrict it to ASCII.

reservedTypeSlugs.description: Words a resource_type slug may never be, because the front end's routes already use them as path segments: /resources/topic/[topic]/ and /resources/[type]/page/[n]/ would collide with a type named topic or page.

typeSlug.description: The slug of a term in the resource_type taxonomy (for example webinar or podcast). A slug, with the reserved words topic and page excluded because they are route segments on the front end.

topicSlug.description: The slug of a term in the resource_topic taxonomy (for example performance). Topics have no reserved words: they only ever appear after the fixed /topic/ segment.

typeList.description: The resource_type terms assigned to a resource. Exactly one: a resource has one type, because the type is a URL segment (/resources/[type]/[slug]/) and a resource has one canonical URL.

topicList.description: The resource_topic terms assigned to a resource, as slugs, each listed once. May be empty: a resource with no topic is still listed at /resources/ and /resources/[type]/.

path.description: A front-end URL path, absolute from the site root, as the front end revalidates it: starts with a single slash and contains no whitespace. A leading // is rejected because it is a protocol-relative URL naming another host, not a path. Listing paths end with a trailing slash (/resources/, /resources/webinar/page/2/).
